label: Take people's stated liking as the evidence I have so far
strong: Judge my rapid prototyping without tests as very successful because the consultant and the beta employees are all excited to start using it to save hours on their end.
Genuinely believe the app we tried hard to build can work, based on the feedback.

label: Learn the hard way what the real difficulty is while building
strong: Find, to my surprise, that the tricky part is not the LLM but reliably capturing the selected text, not messing up the user's clipboard, and inserting the rewrite back without breaking formatting.
Feel glad to have a dialog box with an attached suffix that Just Works, because that is not something I want to fiddle with right now.

label: Push for research against intuition, authority or disinterest
strong: Feel exhausted, as a team, that the developers still tear into a new feature in the meeting after we have all come to an agreement on it.
Think my relationship with the developers was good a year ago but has grown more distant and hostile as our product changes, guided by our research, have grown more ambitious.

label: Decide what a finding means before acting: real problem, novelty, small sample, or noise
strong: Accept ignoring the second finding because my sample size was so small, but judge the first finding a really big problem.
Feel depressed by the user testing results even though I have made changes as a result of them.

label: Hold my ground against opinion by proving it with observed behaviour
strong: Feel glad I held fast to my opinion because it changed an industry for the better.
Decide to let usability testing of our most important tasks guide the design, because I would rather base decisions on actual behavior than on attitudes.

label: Find participants who match my audience
strong: Think the suggestion to forget car-buyer testing and focus on dealership testing is brilliant.
Regret having no access to the huge existing user group that is out there.

label: Hit tools and services that block or price out an individual or a small team
strong: Find every candidate tool either unstable, lacking the necessary features, or horrible in usability.
Find the other tools I looked at not interesting at all.

label: Find that watching people use it reveals what I could never see myself
strong: Discover in usability testing that our users are extremely confused and stare at the page for minutes because the two-field sign-up form does not look like a sign-up form and they assume it is a log-in form despite the large heading.
Feel that qualitative user testing is a wonderful revelation because it quickly flared up UX issues in our product that we had not seen.

label: Fear the problems I have not looked for yet
strong: Feel it really sucks to get an email saying a user can't register for an account.
Find replicating bugs tough with all the variables of OS, PC, browser, location and other oddities.

label: Build what I myself need or find missing
strong: Feel very annoyed by the un-dismissible ads and calls to action in the free Sudoku games I install on my phone.
Feel extra annoyed at failing the challenge of tracking my spending, being a senior finance controller at the time.

label: Hold building, promoting and testing in tension
strong: Feel a little lost over the conflict I feel between acquiring users and developing the product.
Feel uncomfortable with the state of my product and the initial impression it gives visitors, even though the limited feedback from launching is helpful and interesting.

label: Search for a fix after the test exposes a problem the standard guidance does not solve
strong: Feel so disappointed by the result of following aria-live recommendations, which seem to assume page-like content, that I am now searching for any alternatives.
Feel confident we can make the UI understandable, but stumped about using aria-live regions for content that updates more than once per second without the whole experience becoming cacophony.

label: Turn to a community for how-to or validation because I have no reference to lean on
strong: Value the advice from my earlier Ask HN as excellent and take it on board by doing lots of reading and experimenting.
Want tips or validation for pushing back on design feedback that may be completely off-base.

label: Want outside eyes on what I built because I can no longer see it fresh
strong: Feel eager to share my new app with HN.
Find the senior designer's feedback very helpful, with two of his questions really getting me thinking about my process.

label: Weigh whether testing is worth the time and money at all
strong: Feel I am spending unnecessary resources and extending the project timeline when user testing detects the same problems I already found through expert review.

Judge it very worthwhile now to focus on UX enhancements and usability testing, because I am finally a bit freed up from the development grind and traffic has reached a point where even small increases in conversion percentages matter.

label: Realize I built on my own assumptions without a feedback loop, and that early enthusiasm did not predict use
strong: Judge that my cardinal sin was not building a great first base of users to get a feedback loop going.
Realize, after reading The Mom Test, that I did all the wrong things first by building a product expecting people to come without real talks with lead users or a feedback loop.

label: Discount signals that are not observed behaviour: friends' excitement, surveys, ratings, what people say to please me
strong: Feel uncomfortable imposing the UDID hassle of Testflight on future customers because MVP customers differ subtly but significantly from testers.
Recognize the danger that, with me as the designer doing the testing, users will tell me what they expect I want to hear instead of what is actually on their mind.

label: Get the build somewhere people can safely try it
strong: Feel uncomfortable giving our source code away just like that to unknown parties.
Think guerilla testing the TV app would be really inconvenient because bringing a TV to a coffee shop would draw stares.

label: Want to know continuously, in the build loop and in production, whether it works for users
strong: Feel that what we are building is so helpful when a customer’s evals catch small models hallucinating ids that would send a campaign to all their contacts.
Fear degrading MCP performance with our instrumentation, so iterate until the success rate matches running without it.

label: Reconcile what the client or team set up with what I think needs finding out
strong: Feel glad that the client is already bought in to UX research, since it spares me the struggle of selling it.
Worry that changing the already-planned usability tests would seriously inconvenience my client, who has handled the recruiting and logistics so far.

label: Rig up a cheap way to capture what people do
strong: Notice, using the BLU phones side by side with my four-year-old iPhone, a remarkable difference in performance and quality that makes the old iPhone feel like an ultra-luxury rocketship.
Feel eager to test this on people out in the actual field, on site, to get even more ecologically valid data.

label: Reason about whether users will understand, without having watched them
strong: Dislike the label because it is too much noise and clutter that makes identification harder and is not sexy, though I am not UX trained.
s4
Feel the new mockups make it really easy for users to do what they need on the site.

label: Work out the tasks, script and setup so the test is fair
strong: Feel uncomfortable about the script because this is my first time, and would rather give users simple tasks and analysis.
Judge one article's image the best thing I have found while reading, and note the other article only talks about websites, not apps.

label: Build my own tool because nothing does what I need
strong: Feel put off by always having to test every new feature or fix in the browser myself, so I research alternatives.
Decide to build the product because I got tired of doing manual QA for my last SaaS product and did not want to manually test our app.

label: Put it in front of real people early, to learn whether anyone wants it and what breaks
strong: Feel extremely happy with the response and feedback I got from releasing Polls.io probably a little premature.
Decide to develop this further only if there is interest, because I have been burnt building unnecessary stuff before and am now very careful to validate first.

label: Handle what happens in the room: whether to intervene, how long it takes, which devices, which users
strong: Realize I have no good answer when management asks how long the usability test will take, because I have been too busy with scenarios, prototypes, and recruiting to ever consider it.
Disagree immediately with adding mobile-device tasks, but cannot come up with any good explanation why it is a bad thing.

label: Change or simplify the thing because of what people could not get through
strong: Feel unsure which icon to use for the Home tab if all tabs get icons.
Consider adding small icons to the tabs, unsure whether they would help users detect a tab's purpose by hinting at its main action.
